text:
The version-boundary vote needs the current Source/5 and Core/4 constructor sets, not only the candidate prose. I will read those definitions and the completion plan, then vote only on Source/6 → Core/5.**Vote: agree on the Source/6 → Core/5 boundary as a Sprint 0 recommendation. This seat does not freeze it.**

Identity: Grok 4.7 (xAI). The supplied candidate digests were not recomputed here. The worktree texts at the named paths were read. The packet plus those current definitions is enough to vote on the boundary. It is not enough to close W-D0–W-D4, M4-C1 bytes, or Sprint 0.

## Why the boundary is justified

Source/5 binds a closed expression machine and a separate lifecycle kernel. `experiments/moriarty-language/spec/successor/financial-agreement-source-v5.md` lines 6–11 set the Core contract to `moriarty-financial-expression-contract/4` because that constructor set stays closed, and the kernel to `moriarty-financial-lifecycle/1`. Lines 38–39 say the repayment file is a local projection, not authenticated ledger state. `financial-lifecycle.ts` lines 4–6 state the same limit: prepare is not signing, proof, ledger state, or authenticated time.

The expression operand table is closed at `financial-expression-v1.ts` lines 43–87 (`OPERANDS`, `READ_OPERANDS`, `POST_READ_OPERANDS`). `Emit` is one operation id plus a fields expression (line 70). That is not an authenticated multi-party transition.

The lifecycle transfer that Source/5 actually runs is narrower still. `TransferAction` (`financial-lifecycle.ts` lines 85–92) is `from`, one `to`, one `asset`, one `amount`. Allowance is consumed there (lines 1463–1522). `RepayAction` does not move balances itself; it requires a transfer already in the step (lines 1574–1583) and then applies whatever `allocationRule` is stored (`AccrualFirst`, `PrincipalFirst`, or `ProRata`, lines 25 and 1405–1424). A literal-fee stage (debit `v+f`, credit `v`, credit `f`, one signed intent, one head) has no constructor in that kernel. Encoding it as a second `Transfer`, a `Record`, or an `Emit` changes either Source/5 behavior or the meaning of an unauthenticated record.

Obligation amounts are already capped at `signed128Max` `170141183460469231731687303715884105727` (`financial-lifecycle.ts` lines 12–19 and 464–471), which is `2^127−1`. Balances use the full `uint128Max` (line 17). That split is a real compatibility fact. It is not a MIL/4 proof.

`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-29-mil4-k-quint-completion.md` lines 17–19 already require a successor Core when Core/4 cannot represent a required term, and they refuse inherited theorems across a changed state signature. Source/6 → Core/5 matches that rule. Source/5, expression `/4`, lifecycle `/1`, and lifecycle-state `/1` stay as they are.

## What this vote leaves open

`experiments/moriarty-language/formal/mil4/decisions.md` still marks M4-C1 open. The GPT-6 inventory note in that file is not a byte vote. `semantics-contract.md` lines 7–9 correctly keep S0 on proposed `/3` intent bytes and refuse to infer a `/4` signed encoding from the Source/6 or Core/5 labels. The completion plan’s Sprint 2 exit (line 44) asks for canonical `/4` tags. Those are different decisions. This vote covers only the language/Core version boundary.

Sprint 0’s own exit (plan line 42) is unmet: every coverage row is still `unmapped` / `map-or-reject` or `missing` / `to-classify`, and W-D0–W-D4 have no selected bytes, verifier, rejection order, or widths (`semantics-contract.md` lines 36–40 and 64–66).

## Missing constructor classes

The 60 `CORE4:*` names in `coverage.tsv` match the expression `/4` tables. The 48 `SRC5:*` rows match the EBNF left-hand sides. Both inventories stop there. These classes are required by `semantics-contract.md` lines 15–22 and are absent as closed tags:

| Class | Absent closed constructors |
| --- | --- |
| Header | Domain, policy digest, authenticated head, predecessor, validity, stage id, episode id. `MIL4:Header` is one bag. |
| Typed values | No MIL/4 rows. Asset id, domain id, checked `UInt128` quantity, delta, `Price<Base,Quote,Scale>`, shares, position, instant, duration. |
| Intent | Fixed field, permitted cell range, selected branch, gross/fee/net bounds, recipient, surplus, residue. Only `SignedIntent`, `Hole`, and `Fill` exist. |
| Formula | Named rejects for general Φ₁ and uncertified Ω. `CertifiedOmega` has no numeric or cost contract. |
| Authenticated cells | One `AuthenticatedCell`. The contract lists balance, supply, obligation, encumbrance, lock, pool, managed assets, shares, observation, grant, policy, receipt, claim, replay, episode head, tombstone, and profile aggregates. |
| Effects | One `CompleteEffect` and one `RetainedDuty`. No debit, credit, mint, burn, lock, unlock, debt line, claim, receipt, budget use, authority use, work line, or non-posted product remainder. |
| Evidence | One `Evidence`. No policy, selected observation, provenance premise, signer, key, digest, verifier locus, grant scope, epoch, or replay id. |
| Result | `Stage`, `Episode`, `Observation`, `AcceptedFailure`, `AtomicRejection`. No prepared, pending, unknown, recovery, terminal, accepted success, or stable judgment code. |

The lifecycle kernel is missing entirely from `coverage.tsv`: `Transfer`, `Repay`, `Originate`, `Accrue`; effects `Repayment`, `Origination`, `Accrual`; state cells `balances`, `allowances`, `obligations`, four used-id sets, and `work` (`financial-lifecycle.ts` lines 85–139 and 208).

`loan-coll/1` appears in `deliverables/mil4-successor-2026-09-29/DESIGN-MIL4-WORKING.md` and is not one of the eight first profiles. It needs an explicit reject row. The deferred list in `semantics-contract.md` (LP mint/burn, variable credit, rebasing, uncapped options, median/TWAP, general voting, multisigner admission, bonded fast fill, foreign verifier assurance, vault slash, general Φ₁, uncertified Ω) also has no reject rows. The eight `PROFILE:*` rows correctly stay at `FAMILY_STAGE_ADAPTER_ABSENT`.

## Missing source productions

The EBNF left-hand sides in `financial-agreement-source-v5-grammar.ebnf` are all present and all `unmapped`. These productions and alternatives are not:

- `lexical.md` tokens referenced at grammar lines 3–4 and 137–141.
- Header obligations at grammar lines 10–16: the byte, token, AST, depth, declaration, statement, field, argument, and parameter caps, and the `SOURCE_ACTION_COUNT` / post-read placement rules.
- Alternatives inside `primary` (lines 100–112): unary minus, integer, string, `true`, `false`, call, and parentheses.
- Keywords inside `genericCall`, `dynamicOrLiteral`, `financialGeneric`, `financialRead`, and `financialPostRead` (lines 114–131), including `quantity` and the twelve financial read names.
- `comparisonOp` `!=` (line 90). The Core/4 table has `Eq` and `Not` and no `Neq` row, so the lowering is unstated.
- `product` has only `*` (line 94). `FloorDiv` and `CeilDiv` exist on Core/4 and have no Source/5 spelling. Each needs `map` or `reject`, not a shared `map-or-reject`.
- Protected spellings `Transfer`, `Repay`, `Originate`, and `Accrue` (`financial-agreement-source-v5.md` lines 43–45) are semantic constructors, not EBNF left-hand sides, and they are not inventoried.

## Compatibility obligations

Before freeze, the candidate must state all of these as obligations:

1. Source/5 `check`, `format`, `elaborate`, and `evaluate` keep the current profile string and the current Core/4 call.
2. Expression `/4`, lifecycle `/1`, and lifecycle-state `/1` byte and API behavior stay unchanged. A fee field on `TransferAction` would be a Source/5 change.
3. Each lifecycle field is either embedded field-by-field or given a named version rejection. `allocationRule`, `conversion`, `accrualTerms`, `closureReserve`, origination ids, and the four replay sets are part of that list. A generic “legacy record” path is rejected by the candidate’s own rule (`semantics-contract.md` lines 7–8).
4. S0’s identity conversion (`mantissa=1`, `scale=0`, `rounding=none`) and fixed `AccrualFirst` rule are a new Core/5 stage. Lifecycle repay still runs `convertNominal` and can reject `DUST`, and it accepts three allocation rules.
5. S0 local failure publishes no effects. The general constructor may later retain only effects and duties named in a signed failure branch. Those are different branches of one constructor, and the S0 branch is the empty-retain branch.
6. Unknown tags reject. No Source/5 or Core/4 theorem is reused. SP03 files still need a per-file reuse, adapt, archive, or replace disposition (`semantics-contract.md` lines 56–60). `coverage.tsv` still says `map-or-reject`.

## Invalid assumptions to remove before freeze

- A caller-supplied effect hash, `Emit`, or `Record` authenticates omitted endpoints. Expression `/4` does not authenticate ledger state.
- Lifecycle `Repay` plus `Transfer` is already the S0 stage. It is two action ids in one unauthenticated prepare step.
- `LitPrice` (`financial-expression-v1.ts` line 56) is already canonical `Price<Base,Quote,Scale>` for MIL/4. Its Core/4 behavior stays on the old contract; the MIL/4 price still needs its own tag and orientation check.
- The eight family projections are admitted because they have coverage rows. `m4AdmitFamily` rejects them, and `projection.md` defines `α` only for an admitted stage. No Quint run exists.
- Changing the version number selects `/4` wire bytes, a signature scheme, or a verifier locus. W-D1 and W-D2 are open.
- “Checked UInt128” is one width. Obligation fields stop at `2^127−1`; balances may reach `2^128−1`.

## Exact changes before Sprint 0 can freeze

1. In M4-C1, separate “Source/6 and a new Core/5 contract” from “wire generation.” Keep S0 on `/3` until W-D1 and W-D2 select scheme, bytes, digest, and verifier locus.
2. Name the untouched contracts in the boundary paragraph: source `/5`, expression `/4`, lifecycle `/1`, lifecycle-state `/1`.
3. Replace every `map-or-reject` and `to-classify` row with one rule or one named rejection. Add the kernel, lexical, keyword, cell, effect, value, and deferred-profile rows listed above, including `loan-coll/1`.
4. Write the embedding-or-rejection list for lifecycle fields, and state that S0 fee transfer and S0 repay are new Core/5 stages.
5. Record the S0 failure branch as empty-retain, with the signed retained-duty branch left closed until a later profile.
6. Record per-file SP03 dispositions before any Sprint 1 reuse.
7. Keep this vote as one seat. The register still requires a second substantive vote, dissent, and a candidate digest before the row can close.
